Neoblast dynamics during planarian regeneration¶

Miantong Zhang · STAT 530 course project · May 2026

This exploratory reanalysis uses published Schmidtea mediterranea single-cell RNA-seq and Visium data from Cui et al. (2023). It connects temporal changes in neoblast composition with marker profiles and tissue-level spatial context.

The repository edition reorganizes the original course notebook and clarifies its interpretation. The default workflow uses compact tables extracted from the original processed files. Marker rankings were separately recomputed from the provided expression matrix; this notebook displays those results without repeating gene-level testing. See docs/DATA.md for downloads, provenance, and the full-expression workflow.

1. Does the overall sampled neoblast proportion change?¶

Count supplied BigCellType labels at each of eight regeneration time points. Divide the number labeled Neoblast by all sampled cells at that time point. This establishes a descriptive baseline for the subtype analysis.

Neoblasts constitute 23.8% of sampled cells at baseline, 30.4% at 6 hours, 30.1% at 24 hours, and 21.4% at day 7. The sampled fraction therefore rises early and subsequently falls. These proportions alone cannot demonstrate increased absolute stem-cell number, proliferation, or activation.

2. Which annotated neoblast subtypes change over time?¶

Count Annotation labels within the 14,601-cell neoblast dataset and normalize within each time point. Calculate fold change relative to cut0d and rank subtypes by the maximum absolute log2 fold change. The denominator here is all neoblasts, unlike the all-cell denominator in question 1.

Neuronal-biased neoblasts rise from 7.3% at baseline to 15.6% at day 2 and remain relatively high at day 5 (14.5%). The tspan-1+ subtype rises from 15.7% to 23.7% at day 7. Protonephridial-biased neoblasts show the largest relative fold change, from approximately 1.1% to 3.0%, while remaining a small population. Epidermal and muscle/parenchymal subtype fractions are lower at day 7 than at baseline. These are relative composition patterns and do not trace fate transitions.

3. Do annotated subtypes have distinct marker profiles?¶

The full-expression step in scripts/compute_markers.py uses scanpy.tl.rank_genes_groups, with groupby="Annotation", method="wilcoxon", reference="rest", and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. It ranks the 3,000 genes retained in the supplied processed neoblast matrix, pooling time points. Five leading markers from each of five selected subtypes are displayed and matched to a supplied BLAST-symbol lookup.

A reproducibility audit found non-finite or inconsistent profiles in the supplied scaled matrix. The repository marker analysis uses a count-based recovery with the study's normalization/scaling recipe and stored gene-level scaling parameters; see data/processed/matrix_recovery.json. Source files are unchanged. The recovered matrix still contains negative scaled values. Accordingly, this analysis reports ranking scores and adjusted p-values rather than log-fold-change estimates. Marker-panel dot size is the fraction above zero in the supplied matrix, not the fraction with detected RNA; color is the per-gene rescaled mean processed expression. The table below contains saved full-expression results, not marker tests rerun by this notebook.

The selected marker patterns differ across annotated subtypes, supporting transcriptional distinctions between them. Supplied symbol matches include TUBB2B and SOX13 for neuronal-biased cells, and TP63 and SOX11 for epidermal-biased cells. The symbol matches support tentative biological interpretation, not verified cross-species function or lineage identity. Very small cell-level p-values do not substitute for biological-replicate validation.

4. How does overall neoblast representation vary across tissue domains?¶

For each spot in six Visium datasets, divide the provided cell2location_Neoblast estimate by the sum of the seven available cell2location_* major-cell-type estimates. Average these fractions over spots in each supplied STAGATE domain. Merge related gut, body-wall, and epidermal labels. No spatial model is trained here.

For spatial examples at baseline, 24 hours, and day 7, select the library_id with the most spots. One library can contain multiple tissue profiles. Domain summaries include all libraries; examples are not matched longitudinal sections. Missing domain/time combinations remain NaN.

Estimated neoblast fractions differ across tissue domains. The anterior-body average increases from 18.9% at baseline to 42.3% at day 7; body-wall and secretory domains also show relatively high estimates. The day-7 Wounds domain has a mean of 21.8%. Earlier missing Wounds entries indicate missing labels, not proof that wounds were absent.

Only overall neoblast abundance is supplied, so these maps cannot locate individual neoblast subtypes. Tissue-domain patterns provide context for the single-cell results but do not directly map a temporally changing subtype to its tissue destination.

Conclusions and limits¶

The sampled neoblast response has an early increase in relative representation, subtype-specific temporal composition patterns, and spatial variation across tissue domains. These observations motivate the hypothesis that distinct progenitor states participate at different regeneration stages.

The evidence remains descriptive: no replicate-level differential-abundance model, proliferation assay, lineage tracing, subtype-specific spatial deconvolution, or causal perturbation was performed. Existing cell annotations and upstream spatial-model outputs are reused. Spatial domain averages pool spots and do not quantify uncertainty between animals or sections. Interpretation is limited to the supplied processed datasets.

Data and attribution¶

Study: Cui, G. et al. (2023), Nature Communications 14, 3205. DOI. Processed data: OMIX003867. Study code: yangteam repository.

The study authors generated the data, annotations, STAGATE labels, and cell2location estimates. This course project contributes the linked questions, downstream comparisons, marker ranking, and visualizations. Data preparation and full-expression commands are documented in docs/DATA.md.
